statements.text: The ABS Code of Practice for Banks – Credit Cards uses the term 'gross negligence' (paragraphs 5 and 6).
statements.note: 5(a) and 5(c) say 'grossly negligent'; 5(b) and 6 say 'gross negligence'.

statements.text: The code does not define gross negligence and gives no examples of it.
statements.note: Checked against the whole code (11 paragraphs). Paragraph 4 gives card and PIN security advice and does not say that not following it is gross negligence.

statements.text: The code refers to the card issuer finding a cardholder grossly negligent (paragraphs 5(b) and 5(c)). It does not say who must show it.
statements.note: 5(b): 'if a cardholder is found to be grossly negligent'; 5(c): 'In the event that banks find the cardholder grossly negligent'.

statements.text: Under the code a cardholder who has not acted fraudulently or with gross negligence, and who informed the card issuer as soon as reasonably practicable, is liable for no more than S$100 of unauthorised charges before notifying the loss (paragraph 5(a)). Such a cardholder is not liable where the card was not stolen but its details were used for purchases over the telephone or the Internet, or for unauthorised PIN-activated transactions (paragraph 6). A cardholder involved in fraud or who has acted with gross negligence is liable for 100% of the outstanding unauthorised charges (paragraph 5(b)).
statements.note: Reworded from the brief to follow the text: 6(a) is limited to purchases over the telephone or the Internet, 6(b) adds PIN-activated transactions, and 5(b) says '100% of outstanding unauthorised charges'. The code says '$100'.

statements.text: The code is an industry code issued by The Association of Banks in Singapore. It is not legislation.
statements.note: A statement about the document, not a paragraph. It rests on paragraph 1 (compliance with MAS rules) so that it is reviewed with each new version of the code.
